stem: Myasthenia gravis is a condition that results in muscle weakness by affecting the immune response.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *immune response*.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disease which disrupts a cell signalling pathway involving muscle cells.
parts.text: Suggest how the immune system acts to disrupt this cell signalling pathway.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Enzyme **Y** is found in the cell surface membrane of muscle cells. Enzyme **Y** acts to break down the cell signalling molecules which trigger muscle contraction when they are no longer needed.

Using the induced fit hypothesis of enzyme action, explain how enzyme **Y** breaks down the cell signalling molecules.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody used in the treatment of myasthenia gravis.

Rituximab acts against the cell surface membrane protein CD20. This protein is found on the surface of the B-lymphocytes that cause myasthenia gravis.
parts.text: Explain the advantages of using monoclonal antibodies in the treatment of diseases such as myasthenia gravis.
